questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When choosing the destination it was important for me that the university was situated within a city where there were lots to do in weekends, school breaks etc. Also, I choose to study abroad in England as I have family living here and have always had a wish to stay in England for a longer period of time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my stay! Everything was well organised and I really don't have much negative to day about my study abroad experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to find information. If I couldn't find the information I needed, it was easy to find contact information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an optional campus tour just after I arrived, which helped me getting to know the area and meet new people. Also, there was a welcome event for study abroad student after a couple of weeks were I met a lot of new people who became my best friends here.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I had the opportunity to choose between living in a shared house with sharing kitchen and toilets/bathrooms and to choose a studio apartment with my own kitchen and toilet/bathroom.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: As I choose the studio apartment, I had my own kitchen and kitchen equipment. I cooked all my food by myself and I was not offered any catered accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed living on campus as I spend most of my time around campus and it is only a 15-20 minute walk to the city center of Liverpool. There are lots of cafes and pubs around campus which is really great because you don't have to walk into town every time you want to hang out somewhere with your friends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered for my courses before I left my home country and go them accepted just before the start of the semester. I found the module guidance given by the university very helpful when choosing my courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The module guidance showed an overview of the different courses/modules and I choose 50 % of my courses within my field of study and the other 50 % within other departments.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I applied for 6 different modules and got 5 of them pre-approved by the University of Liverpool and finally got accepted to 4 of the modules. I really enjoyed the modules and there were no timetable clashes, so everything worked out really well for me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I applied for modules spread over 3 different departments and one of my biggest concern was timetable clashes. For me this worked out really well and I ended up with two whole days with no teaching, which instead gave me plenty of time to prepare for classes. Therefore, my advice is to just go with whatever you find interesting and try something new within other departments if you wish to.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two year 3 modules (level 3), one year 2 module (level 2) and one year 1 module (level 1).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was surprised with how little teaching there were compared to what I was used to at UCPH. For each module I had 1 hour of lecture and 1 hour of seminar each week which resulted in 8 hours of teaching per week. This resulted in less group work and group assignment however I was very well-prepared for the classes as I had lots of time to prepare.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
COMM301 - NEWS MEDIA AND SOCIETY. 
COMM312 - Introduction to Strategic Communication
202122-MKIB155 - CONSUMER BEHAVIOUR
202122-SOCI213 - Understanding Digital Culture & Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed SOCI213 - Understanding Digital Culture & Society. The teacher was really great and we had very interesting discussions of technologies' impact on society.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is a bit cheaper in the UK than in Denmark. Laundry was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of different societies to join.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All different societies for whatever hobbies or interests the students might have. There a lovely gym that I have used a lot and it even has a swimming pool.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sports club or society, it is a good way to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the cities close to Liverpool, there are really many places worth visiting. I went to Manchester, Leeds, Chester, York, Peak District and the Lake District. I can really recommend trips with wearedaytrippers as they plan day trips departing from Liverpool.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to adjust. Local people were very welcoming and interested in international student.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to as many of the planned events at the beginning of the semester as these were crucial for me to make friends. Also, be open to get to know new people throughout your stay as you will constantly meet people you haven't spoken with previously.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything except that I had to adjust to the Scouse accent that was a bit difficult to understand at first.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I think msot of the culture is similar to Danish culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Consider what is important for you when choosing accommodation on/off campus, studio apartment or shared housing. 
Be aware that you have a lot of teaching-free time during the week, as there are not a lot of hours of teaching. 
Really enjoy it and have an open mind towards all the new people you will meet, it has really been the most amazing experience for me to meet so many people from different countries.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many study abroad students have gone travelling during holiday breaks (we had a three week spring break) and at the end of the semester. It is a good idea to save up money to have the opportunity to go on travels with your new friends.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the campus aspect of the university especially that I only lived 5 minutes from where I had my classes. It was such a lovely atmosphere experiencing all the students living and studying in the same area. Also, I really developed my English language skills which is really rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At the end of the semester I had three really intense exam weeks where I had to write my assignments along with having teaching in my modules right until the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
